bc37eb4adaa770c2: MELAKA: The state government will ensure that every new development, especially residential projects built in Melaka, undergoes a review of the selling price valuation before the project is implemented.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the review will be conducted by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) through the State Land Subdivision and Partition Committee.
He said that the effort needs to be made so that the development carried out is in line with economic growth, job opportunities, housing needs and the people's financial capacity.

"For me, this is not just about the process or approval, but we want the price (of the residence) brought to the market to be truly reasonable, in line with the current value, and still within the reach of buyers.
"The proof, Alhamdulillah, based on the National Property Information Centre Report for the first quarter of this year, Melaka recorded the lowest house sale prices in Malaysia," he said.

He said this while delivering a speech at the inauguration of the Best Data Supplier Appreciation Ceremony of the National Property Information Centre (NAPIC) and the What's New Property Information System Malaysia 2.0 Southern Zone Seminar, which was also attended by JPPH director-general Datuk Abdul Razak Yusak.

Ab Rauf said that in the first six months of this year, Melaka recorded 8,661 real estate transactions worth RM3.1 billion, with the residential subsector remaining the main contributor via 5,479 transactions worth RM1.78 billion.
He said the housing affordability ratio in Melaka is around 3.27 compared to the national average of 4.39, but this achievement is not a licence for the state government to feel complacent.
He also said the challenge that needs to be faced is ensuring that the level of affordability can be maintained as the market, development costs, and people's needs continue to change.

"The state government aims to increase the home ownership rate to 88 per cent by 2030, and we want more people in Melaka not just to dream of owning a home, but to finally hold the keys to their own house.
"For me, that is the true measure of the success of a housing policy, not how many houses we approve or build, but how many people can truly afford to own them," he added.
6f6fb666e9bcbf2c: KUALA LUMPUR: The police are open to helping the Health Ministry (MOH) operate mercy flights to transport patients requiring emergency treatment from remote areas.

Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, however, said the air operations force currently faced constraints in terms of available air assets, given the vast operational area it covered nationwide.
He said the police currently had only two fixed-wing aircraft and one helicopter available in Sarawak.
"While the need may be quite urgent at this moment, I believe this is something we can consider for the future and to foster better cooperation with the ministry concerned.

"Perhaps through the acquisition of new assets or other means, we can facilitate collaboration between the ministry and agencies to ensure that their duties and responsibilities are carried out more effectively in the future," he said.
He said this at a press conference after the Senior Police Officer Rank Insignia Presentation and Handover of Duties Ceremony at the Kuala Lumpur Police Training Centre (Pulapol) here today.

It was previously reported that Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said four government agencies would assist MOH in operating mercy flights to ensure residents in remote areas requiring medical treatment continued to have access to healthcare services.

The temporary mercy flight services will be provided pending completion of the investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Miri, Sarawak, on Sept 8, in which the aircraft caught fire.
On the progress of the crash investigation, Khalid expressed his condolences to the victims' families and said police had so far recorded statements from 20 witnesses.
He said additional statements would be recorded before the investigation papers were completed.

Meanwhile, Khalid said police were finalising their investigation into a report lodged by Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, who claimed he had been coerced into signing the Proclamation Instrument seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
He said the matter was sensitive and required thorough scrutiny, taking into account not only the police investigation but also the customs and traditions of Negri Sembilan.
"We are still preparing the investigation papers and may require further action, as well as input from the Attorney General's Chambers and other relevant parties," he said.
Ismail had claimed he was forced to sign the document before lodging a police report on Sept 8 to enable the authorities to investigate the matter.
66d21ac1dbb2f302: PORT DICKSON, Sept 15 — The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions.

“I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad. There are currently 24 million MyKad cards in circulation, with an average of 180,000 to 200,000 cards issued each month,” he told reporters here today.
He said the replacement of the MyKad would not affect subsidy balances or eligibility for subsidies linked to the identity card.
“There is no issue regarding the subsidy balance...the records are based on the existing MyKad,” he said.

Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said the department handles between 13,000 and 15,000 cases of unregistered births each year, a figure he described as still high even though Malaysia gained independence decades ago.
He said failure to register births was due to various factors, including lack of information, social problems and family issues, which could ultimately affect the children’s future.

“The reality is that there are still people who lack the basic knowledge that every birth must be registered, and this is still regarded as something normal,” he said, adding that parents or guardians gave various reasons for failing to register their children’s births, including financial difficulties and family constraints, even though birth registration is free.
In this regard, he urged parents, guardians and members of the public with information on unregistered births to come forward to NRD offices for assistance. — Bernama
6d4359d6085d93bc: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must strengthen its care economy to help more women enter or return to the workforce, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.

Delivering her keynote address at the 5th Malaysia Sustainability Leadership Summit today, she said 42.8 per cent of the 4.89 million women outside the labour force cited domestic responsibilities and caregiving as their main reason for staying out of the workforce.
She said that caregiving had long been treated as a private family matter, borne disproportionately by women and often without formal recognition, training or adequate support.

"Nearly one million women in Malaysia are both the primary caregiver and sole breadwinner in their households. Many are single mothers, and only a proportion are connected to formal social protection systems.
"This is not a question of talent or capability. It is a structural gap that prevents our economy from fully benefiting from women's skills and potential," she said.
She said the issue was reflected in Malaysia's female labour force participation rate, which stood at 56.6 per cent in 2025, significantly lower than the 83.3 per cent recorded for men.
She said the figures showed that more needs to be done to remove barriers preventing women from participating fully in the labour market, particularly those related to caregiving responsibilities.
"Malaysia cannot realise its full economic potential while half of its talent pool remains underutilised. Hence, women's economic participation remains a major opportunity," she said.
She said the ministry is implementing the Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan 2026–2030 as a national roadmap to professionalise, regulate and expand a sustainable care ecosystem.

She said the framework sets out the strategic direction for improving the quality, affordability and accessibility of childcare and eldercare, while strengthening recognition and training for caregivers.

"A well-structured care economy can create quality employment, professionalise caregiving, support women who wish to enter or return to the workforce, and open new opportunities for social enterprises and businesses."
Nancy said addressing the issue also requires stronger collaboration between the government, businesses, civil society, communities and academia through a Public-Private-People Partnership (4P).

She emphasised that businesses should increasingly view family-friendly policies, care infrastructure and flexible work arrangements as investments in productivity, talent retention and sustainable business performance, rather than mere corporate social responsibility initiatives.
Furthermore, she said Malaysia's ageing population, evolving family structures and changing economic pressures on households require more urgent and precise responses.

She called on organisations participating in the summit to identify at least one concrete cross-sector collaboration arising from the event, with clear deliverables and measurable outcomes for the year ahead.

The 5th Malaysia Sustainability Leadership Summit convened about 130 policymakers, government officials, business and sustainability leaders, civil society representatives and community leaders to strengthen collaboration and speed up Malaysia's progress towards the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
9163f22660c07998: KUALA LUMPUR: KL City defender Giancarlo Gallifuoco's dream of representing Malaysia remains on hold, with the Australian-born centre-back still waiting for an update on his naturalisation process.

Gallifuoco has fulfilled the five-year requirement to qualify for naturalisation after playing in Malaysia since joining KL City in February 2021, but unlike Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) duo Bergson Da Silva and Brad Tapp, he remains in limbo.
The FA of Malaysia announced on Monday that FIFA had confirmed Bergson and Tapp are eligible to represent Harimau Malaya, leaving Gallifuoco hoping his own wait will eventually bring similar news.
"Congratulations to Bergson and Brad Tapp. I am sure it is their dream, just like it is mine. Unfortunately, I still don't know anything," said the 32-year-old.
"I hope I can give you some good news and say, 'yes, I can represent Harimau Malaya too'.
"I am still waiting for good news, but until now, there has been nothing."
Gallifuoco revealed the wait has already cost him one opportunity he had dreamed of, having hoped to make his Malaysia debut against Vietnam in March.
"Actually, my dream was to play against Vietnam in March. Unfortunately, I also had to cancel the tickets I had already bought for my mother and father," he said.
The defender had been so hopeful of being involved that he had already made plans for his parents to be there, only for the opportunity to pass without a resolution to his naturalisation status.
With the FIFA Asean Cup coming up from Sep 21-Oct 6, Gallifuoco is now less optimistic about getting his chance to don the Harimau Malaya jersey.
"As for September, I also feel I will not be able to play," he said.
The status of two other JDT naturalised players, Manuel Hidalgo and Shane Lowry, also remains under review, with FAM still waiting for an official decision from FIFA.
2ef3a3dd0368eb2c: LOS ANGELES, Sept 15 — The brightest stars in television hit the red-carpet Monday for the Emmy Awards, television’s equivalent of the Oscars, and they certainly gave fashion fans something to talk about.
Here are some of the top looks seen at the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles:
All the sparkles
The women of Hollywood know that under the bright lights, a bit of shimmer goes a long way.

Zendaya, who often turns heads with her red-carpet flair, glistened in a custom silver Prada gown featuring a plunging neckline and plenty of bling — crystals embroidered into the dress and diamonds in her ears.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Zendaya in a custom silver Prada gown. — AFP pic
A sassy short haircut completed the look for the actress, a past winner who is again a nominee for her work on Euphoria.
Selena Gomez, a nominee for best comedy actress for Only Murders in the Building, oozed glamour in a strapless gold column gown from Louis Vuitton, her hair long, loose and curly.

Host Mariska Hargitay, already a two-time Emmy winner this year for her documentary My Mom Jayne, looked radiant in a glittering fire engine red, curve-hugging Monse gown that cascaded to the floor in a fringed train.
Her daughter Amaya wore a matching look, with both appearing to channel the spirit of Hargitay’s mother, late movie icon Jayne Mansfield.
Soft pastels
Other stars at the Peacock Theatre opted for softer looks, in dreamy hues of green, lavender and pale blue.

Elle Fanning, the star of Apple TV’s quirky Margo’s Got Money Troubles who is nominated alongside Gomez, rocked a sleeveless sparkling green Ralph Lauren slip dress with a shoulder tassel that trailed to the floor.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Elle Fanning. — AFP pic
Katherine LaNasa, last year’s winner for best drama supporting actress for The Pitt, and a nominee again this time around, was a vision in a simple sky-blue Louis Vuitton gown with spaghetti straps.

And Sarah Pidgeon, a nominee for the much-talked-about limited series Love Story: John F Kennedy Jr & Carolyn Bessette, stunned on the peacock blue carpet — in celebration of NBC’s 100th anniversary — wearing a purple Chanel slip dress with silver bead and pearl accents.
Dapper men
The Emmys usually does not deliver an adventurous red carpet, especially for the guys, but a few stood out.
Colman Domingo, a double nominee for his work on Euphoria and The Four Seasons, is always raising the fashion bar for Hollywood’s men, and he did not disappoint.
He wore a soft brown Valentino jacket with a Mandarin collar and knob buttons, a sassy fuchsia sash belt fastened with an elaborate silver brooch and fluid cream trousers.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Colman Domingo. — AFP pic
Noah Wyle, who won for the second year in a row for best drama actor for his gritty medical drama The Pitt, donned a tan tuxedo jacket with silky lapels and black trousers from Brunello Cucinelli.
Dress the part
If you want to win an Emmy, you need to...dress like an Emmy?

Megan Stalter attends the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at Peacock Theatre on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. — AFP pic
She showed up in a gold midriff-baring top and hot pants, gold body paint, necklaces, wings and carrying an atom, exactly like the winged woman statuette she hopes to take home. — AFP
eaae9fd5024f0078: KUCHING: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today paid a courtesy call on Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar to present an official invitation to the Malaysia Day celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) tomorrow night.
Fahmi said the visit also provided an opportunity to brief Wan Junaidi on final preparations for the celebration, which is scheduled to run from 8.15pm to about 10.30pm.
"Alhamdulillah, the courtesy call went very well. Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah and I presented the invitation to Tun for tomorrow's celebration.

"All preparations are progressing well. There are a few technical aspects that will be fine-tuned and, insya-Allah, the event will run smoothly," he told reporters after the courtesy call at Astana Negeri Sarawak.

Also present were Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister and Minister-in-Charge of the Malaysia Day 2026 celebration Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, and Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Fahmi said that during the hour-long meeting, Wan Junaidi also shared some of his extensive experience, particularly from his time serving in the police.

Fahmi said he also updated Wan Junaidi on the publication of a special book about the Governor by the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), as well as several related programmes, including a thanksgiving ceremony at the State Mosque and a Malaysia Day exhibition organised by the Information Department.
About 5,000 people are expected to attend the Malaysia Day celebration at BCCK tomorrow night.
Wan Junaidi and his wife, Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi, are expected to attend, along with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
3c84511f58a3c0d3: PUTRAJAYA: The Northern Corridor Economic Region (NCER) is seeking more balanced and strategic allocations under Budget 2027 to spur development in less-developed areas of the northern region and support growth in sectors beyond manufacturing.

Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA) chief executive Datuk Mohamad Haris Kader Sultan said Budget 2027 should give greater attention to less-developed areas, while ensuring development in the northern region remains balanced and strategic.

"We hope that the Budget 2027 allocations will be directed towards the northern regions, particularly the less developed areas. It is important to have fair, balanced, and strategic funding for these parts of the north," he said during a media briefing on the NCER Strategic Development Plan here today.
Mohamad Haris said NCER's expectation was linked to its NCER Strategic Development Plan 2026-2030, with Budget 2027 seen as an opportunity to support development in the northern region further.

He said that manufacturing continues to dominate the region, with expected growth. Therefore, greater attention should also be given to other sectors, particularly tourism and agriculture, in Budget 2027.
"We hope that besides manufacturing, the tourism and agriculture sectors should also be given attention in the northern region
"The focus on these sectors is expected to complement the region's existing manufacturing base while ensuring that development extends to areas that are less developed," said Mohamad Haris.
Earlier, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir launched the NCER 2026-2030 Strategic Development Plan.

The plan is aimed at realising a cumulative investment of RM470 billion by 2030 (in the northern region), with 70 per cent of it contributed by key sectors such as electrical and electronics, automotive, high-value tourism and modern agriculture.
The target set is RM126.2 billion higher than the RM343.8 billion under the previous NCER development plan.

The new plan also aims to increase the gross domestic product of the northern region to RM369 billion; create 310,000 job opportunities, including 45 per cent high-skilled jobs; and raise the median household income to RM7,500.
Budget 2027, scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9, is the fifth MADANI Budget, and it seeks to build on the gains of the Economy MADANI framework and carry Malaysia forward.
As the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan, it is guided by three priorities, namely Raising the Ceiling, Raising the Floor, and Driving Reform in Governance.
cc6b6bb0c3ba1b24: RAWANG: Prominent lawyer Mohamed Haniff Khatri Abdulla and his family escaped with their lives but were left with almost nothing after fire tore through their Bandar Country Homes home early today.

The blaze, which broke out around 3am, destroyed belongings and memorabilia accumulated by the family over 28 years, including handwritten notes and journals Haniff had kept for more than three decades.
Haniff said his daughter spotted flames in the living room on the second floor after leaving her bedroom to get a drink of water.
He was downstairs watching the Leeds United-Newcastle United football match when she alerted him.
Haniff grabbed half a pail of water and tried to put out the flames, but quickly abandoned the effort as the fire spread and thick smoke filled the area.
"The fumes were already in my mouth, were already in my throat.
"It was so hot, I felt a bit of a burn," he said to the New Straits Times.
The family of four fled the house as objects began exploding and glass shattered around them.
Haniff escaped with a minor burn, which was treated by firefighters at the scene.
"They (the Fire and Rescue Department) came with their own first-aid kit. When I realised there was a bit of burn... they helped me," he told the New Straits Times.
Firefighters arrived within 10 minutes, but by then much of the family's belongings had been destroyed.
Pages from books were scattered across the upper floor among charred debris, while clothes, beds, home appliances and other possessions were reduced to ash.
Among the items lost were Haniff's handwritten notes and journals, which he had kept for more than 30 years.
His son, Mohamed Hamzah Khatri Mohamed Haniff, found a PSP console on the floor of his bedroom, one of the few recognisable belongings left behind.
He was also hoping his graduation photographs from three years ago could be salvaged.
"My graduation photos were in my room when the fire happened," Hamzah said.
The family was also unable to locate their cats after the blaze.
Hamzah said two recently adopted kittens were believed to have been in his sister's room when the fire broke out.
Only a pet carrier and a packet of cat food remained visible near the entrance of the house.
Haniff and his family had lived in the house since 1998, moving there when his eldest daughter was just two and a half years old.
"So we have stayed here for 28 years. My daughter, the eldest one, was two and a half years old when we moved here," he said.
Despite losing almost everything, father and son said they were accepting of what had happened and would focus on rebuilding their lives.
"At least everyone is safe. That's the most important thing.
"These items, it's all secondary. Life is more important," Hamzah said.
Haniff said the family had also come to terms with the loss.
"As Muslims, we have to redha," he said.

2ee4e3e58da23ef8: KUALA LUMPUR: Aaron Chia has conquered the world before — with Soh Wooi Yik as his partner. Now with a different partner, he hopes to conquer the Asian Games, which start on Saturday.
Aaron, 29, believes he and Tee Kai Wun, despite being a scratch pairing, are up to scratch for the Asiad mission.
Although they are a new combination, Aaron does not see it as a disadvantage, but a strength instead.
Aaron, who won the world title with Wooi Yik in 2002 in Tokyo, feels that playing as a scratch pair will free them from the weight of expectations carried by the established pairs.

"We're definitely hoping that we can win a medal for Malaysia. We're going there as a scratch pair, so perhaps the others will have more pressure than us. I think that could be an advantage for us," said Aaron on Tuesday.
"I think being a scratch pair is an advantage because some of the top pairs may not know our style of play yet."
It is worth noting that at the Doha 2006 Asian Games, a pair of new faces from Malaysia then, Koo Kien Keat-Tan Boon Heong stunned the field to win the gold.
"We're going there (Asian Games) as underdogs. I think that allows us to play more calmly and with less pressure. So, hopefully, we can have a breakthrough there," said Aaron.
Aaron won a bronze medal with Wooi Yik at the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games, but Wooi Yik was dropped by BAM from the 2026 Asiad in favour of Kai Wun.
Aaron said the fact that some of the top pairs have yet to play against him and Kai Wun could work in their favour.
Aaron-Kai Wun's only international experience as a pair was at the Thomas Cup in Horsens, Denmark in April, where they beat Japan's Kakeru Kumagai-Hiroki Nishi (wirkd No. 21) in three games.

In Nagoya, the Malaysian scratch pair will battle it out with rivals like South Korea's world No. 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, Indonesia's world No. 2 Fajar Alfian-Shohibul Fikri and China's world No. 3 Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang.

Though the world's top three men's pairs will compete in Japan, leaving Aaron-Kai Wun with a mountain to climb, higher than Mt Fuji, Aaron-Kai Wun are undaunted. They see themselves as contenders. And as underdogs, compatriots Kien Keat-Boon Heong have scaled such height before.
"They are regulars on the World Tour, so I don't think there will be much difference there," said Aaron.
Malaysia have not won an Asian Games gold medal in badminton since Kien Keat-Boon Heong's 2006 triumph, and BAM hope to end the 20-year wait this time.
If Aaron-Kai Wun surprise with a gold medal in Ichinomiya City, it will also justify BAM doubles head coach Herry IP's controversial doubles reshuffle experiment.

68476cad68caec28: MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will discuss with national oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) a Maldivian proposal for oil exploration, as Malaysia looks to expand economic cooperation with the island nation.
Anwar said he would raise the proposal with Petronas, noting the company's extensive international experience in oil and gas exploration and operations.

"I will have to discuss this with Petronas. I believe the strength of Petronas now is throughout the world, from Canada to Turkmenistan to Sudan, Suriname, Peru and Brazil. I don't think it's too much of a problem to come closer here to Maldives.
"At least, if they are not able to explore oil, they can at least rest a few days here," he said at a joint press conference with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu today.
He said Malaysia was also prepared to work with the Maldives on climate change, an issue of particular importance to the climate-vulnerable island nation.

Anwar criticised the shortfall in climate financing commitments by developed countries and said Malaysia and the Maldives should work together to push for the implementation of earlier COP decisions, including financing.
He said addressing climate change and implementing effective programmes would require additional funds.
0dc523195f197b80: SYDNEY: Australian far-right leader Pauline Hanson offered a rare but qualified apology on Tuesday after she described the country's Indigenous people as "primitive".
For years a political outsider, Hanson's One Nation has surged this year to become one of Australia's most popular parties, according to opinion polls.

Long known for racist and inflammatory statements about minorities, Hanson drew outrage from across the political spectrum on Monday for describing Indigenous Australians as the "most primitive race on Earth".
She told reporters in Canberra on Tuesday that "if I've offended people by using that, then I will apologise for that".
The senator for Queensland said in a separate interview with News24 that she was "not the most eloquent speaker".
"I've always put my foot in my mouth in the way I come out and say things," she said.
"I regret saying that because I don't want to upset people. That wasn't my intention to hurt people."
Indigenous Australians, whose ancestors have lived on the continent for more than 60,000 years, have average life expectancies about eight years shorter than the rest of the population.
Several factors contribute to the disparity, with chronic health issues, higher poverty rates, more limited access to healthcare in some communities and complex socio-economic causes often blamed.
Indigenous people are also far more likely to be incarcerated or die in custody than other Australians.
Hanson also said on Tuesday she was sorry if she had offended Prime Minister Anthony Albanese with recent comments in which she disparaged the leader's late mother for living in public housing.
Albanese condemned the "mean and nasty" remarks, which sparked calls from an opposition lawmaker to "leave mums out of it".
Hanson's long history of provocative comments appears to have done little to dent her popularity.

An opinion poll conducted by Resolve Strategic on behalf of The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age newspapers released on Sunday showed 27% of Australians would vote for Hanson's party -- one percentage point behind the ruling Labor Party.
a437276fa8ea188e: PUTRAJAYA: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry will not compromise on any management weaknesses or non-compliance that could affect public interest within its agencies and subsidiaries.
Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the ministry will continue to strengthen oversight of governance, integrity and financial management across all its agencies and subsidiaries.
"I want every organisation under the ministry to be managed transparently, with integrity, and in full compliance with the rules and procedures set out.
"Any weakness in management, non-compliance or matter that could affect public interest must be identified and acted upon accordingly," he said in a statement today.
He said agencies and subsidiaries must also ensure that every decision, procurement and use of public funds is carried out responsibly and accountably.
He said people's trust must be safeguarded and every ringgit of public money must be managed well.
It was reported that the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission is conducting probe on probe into delayed fertiliser supplies to some padi farmers in Kedah.

MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said investigators had been instructed to conduct a comprehensive probe covering everyone involved in the policy, tender and implementation of the supply process.
f32b3a3fa56af022: KUALA LUMPUR: National men's singles coach Tey Seu Bock is hopeful his four charges will rise to the challenge and produce their best at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games from Sept 19 to Oct 4.
World No. 31 Leong Jun Hao, Justin Hoh (No. 45), Eogene Ewe (No. 82) and Kong Wei Xiang (No. 242) will compete in the men's singles at the prestigious multi-sport Games.

The national men's singles squad has endured a challenging period in recent months, with inconsistent performances on the international stage, particularly involving Jun Hao, who holds the status of Malaysia's No. 1 player.

Seu Bock has not only placed emphasis on the technical and tactical aspects of their game but also on ensuring they are mentally prepared to handle the pressure of competing at a major event like the Asiad.

"Our preparations are in good shape and I hope they can perform well in Japan. The players are also in good mental and physical condition," Seu Bock said at the Academy Badminton Malaysia (ABM) on Tuesday.
Malaysia will begin their men's team event campaign on Sept 20, while the individual competition starts on Sept 25.
Malaysia have been on a 56-year gold drought at the Asian Games since Datuk Punch Gunalan's triumph at the 1970 edition in Bangkok.
The nation's best opportunity came at the 2010 Guangzhou Games, where Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei had to settle for silver after losing to two-time Olympic champion Lin Dan of China in the final.

Jun Hao and Justin will compete in the individual event from Sept 25-29, where Thailand's world No. 3 Kunlavut Vitidsarn and China's world No. 6 Shi Yu Qi will be among the title contenders at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium in Ichinomiya City.
a6fd5baf9bbac7c0: PUTRAJAYA: Long before he rose to the highest judicial office in the country, the late Tun Mohamed Dzaiddin Abdullah began his working life in a newsroom.
Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh said Dzaiddin's unusual journey through journalism, policing and law may have given him a broader understanding of justice.
"Perhaps that breadth of experience explains his gift.
"He understood justice not only as judges see it but also through the eyes of the public.
"In my humble view, Dzaiddin taught the Judiciary to listen again," he said during reference proceedings held in memory of four late senior judges at the Federal Court here today.
Dzaiddin began his working life in 1956 as a journalist with the Malay Mail before joining the police force as an inspector.
It was during his time in the police force that former Lord President Tun Mohamed Suffian Mohamed Hashim encouraged him to pursue a career in law.
His journey to the Bench began in 1979 when he was appointed a part-time judicial commissioner, sitting in the Kuala Lumpur and Penang High Courts.
Dzaiddin was elevated to the Supreme Court in 1993 before reaching the pinnacle of his judicial career on Dec 20, 2000, when he was appointed Chief Justice.

Meanwhile, Attorney-General (A-G) Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Dzaiddin's judicial legacy included decisions that underscored the role of the courts in ensuring that the exercise of public power remained within the law.
He cited *Mohamad Ezam Mohd Noor and Others v Ketua Polis Negara*, which concerned the detention of several people under the Internal Security Act 1960.
Dusuki said the decision affirmed the judiciary's role in scrutinising the exercise of public power and ensuring that such powers remained subject to the law.
It was in recalling that case that the A-G stressed the principle that no public authority was beyond legal scrutiny.
"No public power is absolute. Every criminal investigation and detention must be undertaken bona fide and in strict accordance with the law.
"His legacy lives on in the standards he upheld, the confidence he helped nurture, the institutional relationships he strengthened, and the vision he offered for the future of our courts," he added.
d979633ede9838ad: KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Pacific will need 19,120 new passenger aircraft over the next 20 years, of which about 6,373 will be for fleet replacement and the remaining 12,747 to support airline growth, according to Airbus' latest Global Market Forecast (GMF) for 2026-2045.
Airbus said demand in Asia Pacific represents 45 per cent of the total global demand for 42,060 new aircraft over the next two decades.
"Of the 19,120 new passenger aircraft needed over the next two decades in the Asia Pacific region, one-third will be for replacement and the remainder for growth.

"Driving this growth are robust economic fundamentals. By 2045, the middle-income population in Asia Pacific is projected to reach three billion people. Coupled with rapid urbanisation, air travel is increasingly becoming the essential lifeline for social and economic prosperity," Airbus said in a statement today.
Asia Pacific is also expected to account for the largest share of global widebody deliveries, with demand for 3,420 new aircraft, representing almost half of all new widebody aircraft.
Airbus said it is well positioned to meet the region's widebody jet requirements with its A330neo and A350 families.

"Together, the two product lines have seen Airbus increase its share of the widebody backlog in the region to 50 per cent over the past three years, with the A350 now firmly established as the preferred choice of airlines in the region for long-range intercontinental flights," it said.
The European planemaker added that the A350-1000 has emerged as the natural successor to the Boeing B777-300ER.
As for narrowbody aircraft, Airbus forecast that Asia Pacific would need 15,700 aircraft in the 100-244-seat category by 2045.
Airbus said the demand reflects continued domestic and intra-regional network expansion, driven by fleet replacement and long-term capacity growth.

The manufacturer also said new airport infrastructure and longer-range single-aisle aircraft such as the A321XLR and A220 are enabling airlines to open new city pairs, bypass traditional mega-hubs and connect secondary cities.
Airbus said the A220 has created more than 400 new routes globally, while it sees potential for the aircraft to open more than 800 new unserved city pairs in Asia Pacific.

Airbus Asia Pacific president Anand Stanley said airlines are decentralising beyond traditional hub-and-spoke models to connect secondary cities directly to the global economy, while also expanding their long-haul networks.
"By leveraging latest-generation aircraft technology, carriers in the region are rewriting connectivity maps and driving the region's long-term economic prosperity," he said.

Airbus said passenger traffic in Asia Pacific is forecast to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 5.1 per cent, compared with the global average of 3.9 per cent, with traffic volumes expected to more than double by 2045.
As at end-August 2026, 119 airlines in Asia Pacific operated 5,000 Airbus commercial aircraft, giving the manufacturer a 58 per cent market share.
Airbus said nearly 3,500 of its aircraft are also on order for future delivery, representing 61 per cent of the backlog among all aircraft manufacturers in the above-100-seat jet market.
352b146b2b823cce: TOKYO: The fate of the sharpest yen rally in 18 months rests on the Bank of Japan breaking free of its cautious rate-hiking path, though it risks a sharp reversal if the currency again succumbs to the forces that dragged it to 40-year lows in July.

A sudden, more hawkish tone to central bank rhetoric at the start of the month — with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling on the BOJ to "do the right thing" — triggered a blistering 5% surge in the yen against the dollar.
Yen buying was reinforced by growing speculation that Japan's US$2 trillion government pension fund might lead the repatriation of large amounts of capital to invest it at home.

But following the yen's climb to a nearly seven-month high at 152.89 per dollar last week on bets that the BOJ will double the pace of rate hikes to once per quarter — climbing above 2% a year from now versus 1% at present — analysts say risks are heavily skewed towards a market disappointment at Friday's policy decision.

"Even if the BOJ hikes this time, it will be hard for the BOJ to be more hawkish than what the market expects," said Masafumi Yamamoto, chief currency strategist at Mizuho Securities in Tokyo, while flagging the risk of a retreat toward 157 yen per dollar.
"The market is pricing in too much. Above 2% for the terminal rate is too high. It will damage the Japanese economy."
And a ramp-up in bets for Federal Reserve tightening, following inflation data last week that showed a broadening of price pressures, threatens to bolster the dollar at the yen's expense.

The market now sees a Fed hike on Wednesday as a near certainty, with rates then rising once per quarter over the next 12 months, meaning that the hawkish BOJ wagers that have boosted the yen are "totally cancelled out," Yamamoto said.

Both central banks tightening policy in parallel should keep the yield gap on 10-year bonds at a gaping 200 basis points — one of the fundamental drivers of yen weakness against the dollar for much of the past decade.
Another is Japan's worsening terms of trade, with the country's dependence on imported oil underscored by the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The stage could be set for traders to rapidly rebuild positions in so-called carry trades, where investors borrow cheaply in Japan to buy higher-yielding assets elsewhere, following a massive unwinding during the yen's rally.
Shorts flushed
By one measure, those trades stood at a record high at the start of the month.
In the aftermath, speculative positioning in the yen flipped to be net long for the first time since February, according to the latest Commodity Futures Trading Commission data.
However, analysts take the flushing out of many of those positions as a bearish signal for the yen, because it creates room for speculators to rebuild short positions.
And with optimism over US-centred AI trades still intact, Japanese money is also likely to continue to flow to Wall Street, the analysts said.

Japanese investors made their biggest shift toward overseas equities in five months in August, pouring 1.3 trillion yen (US$8.4 billion) into foreign shares, the finance ministry's monthly dataset showed on Sept 8.
However, some investors are now positioning for an expected flow of funds into Japan that could amount to hundreds of billions of dollars.
Pension pivot

Speculation that Japan's Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) could be preparing to invest more heavily in domestic stocks and bonds swirled last week after it released the minutes of a recent meeting of its governing board.

Commentators pointed to the unusual timing of the meeting — during the summer holidays — and the fact that "the basic portfolio" topped the agenda. Discussions on the same topic in March concluded that no review was necessary.

What had changed in the interim was that Japan's benchmark 10-year bond yields had soared some 100 basis points to higher than 3% for the first time in three decades. And in July, both Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama called on pension funds to invest more at home.
A GPIF spokesperson declined to comment on the speculation, but said the fund assesses its portfolio annually.
Analysts, though, generally consider market expectations to be overblown, in terms of both the likelihood and impact of any allocation changes.
GPIF's governance framework requires it to minimize its impact on the market, meaning that any shift would be spread out over a period of months.

Koichi Sugisaki, Morgan Stanley's head of Japan macro strategy, said that any repatriation would "only be a temporary flow, much like forex intervention," and would not alter fundamentals that point to a yen rate of 167 per dollar.
That is if the repatriation story even plays out.
Even with Japanese yields standing at around 3%, returns would fall well short of the GPIF's target return of 1.9% plus nominal wage growth, which Morgan Stanley puts at between 3% and 3.5%.
"GPIF has little incentive to increase its allocation to domestic bonds," Sugisaki said.
48c70c79c7cdc03c: CHINA and Nepal have taken different approaches to information after a Himalayan flood, shaping what the public saw of a disaster that killed more than 1,400 people.
The Aug 26 tsunami-like surge of water, mud and debris from a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border left more than 5,650 missing, including hundreds of foreigners.
Both China and Nepal have gone after fabricated posts on the flood.
But Beijing has gone further to suppress eyewitness video footage and punish people challenging official figures.

Information transmitted by Chinese state media on the flood gave little voice to the missing people's relatives and focused on emergency workers' recovery efforts in Tibet, where foreign journalists do not enjoy unfettered access.

Nepal has pressured social media platforms and news outlets to remove fabricated visuals – including some debunked by AFP fact-checkers – but Kathmandu offers regular updates of death tolls via social media.
Direct commentary from families of victims is readily available on and offline.
Umesh Shrestha, chair of the independent regulatory body Press Council Nepal, said it had asked more than 100 social media accounts to remove content. Most obeyed.
"Things can spread very quickly," Shrestha said.
Nepali police arrested one man who allegedly shared a fabricated donation to a relief fund to promote his personal account.
The disaster came just ahead of the one-year anniversary of anti-corruption protests that toppled the previous government, triggered by a social media ban.
China penalised 10 people accused of spreading falsehoods online, according to the Ministry of Public Security.
They include some who allegedly suggested the actual death toll was higher than official figures.
Beijing's foreign ministry insists the release of information has been "open, transparent and timely", and criticised what it has called "malicious smearing and sensationalism."
It also organised a trip for a small number of foreign media to the Tibetan epicentre of the disaster.
AFP fact-checkers have debunked dozens of claims about the floods in multiple languages.
One video that falsely claimed to show the glacial and mountain collapse that caused the flooding – posted on Facebook and X – was filmed in Alaska's Columbia Glacier days beforehand.
Other footage created using Google's AI tools showed water breaching a riverbank and flooding streets and amassed tens of thousands of interactions.
"During disasters, public panic is high," said Nepali investigative journalist Rabi Raj Baral, who is also a member of the Press Council Nepal.
But both Nepal and China have not only gone after fabrications, but have also targeted posts including some sharing genuine footage.
Nepali authorities have held talks with Meta and TikTok to speed up the removal of AI content, graphic images and fraudulent aid schemes.
Both platforms pay AFP to fact-check posts with potentially false information.
Video verified by AFP as showing the deluge engulfing Gyirong Port – the border post with Nepal – and other eyewitness content have largely disappeared from the Chinese internet.
Social media sites such as Douyin and Weibo have instead featured extensive state media coverage of search operations, without naming the missing or showing much footage of families' reactions.
AFP fact-checkers found flood-related misinformation is mostly absent from Chinese platforms, although conspiracy theories have blossomed abroad.

Posts shared from Canada to South Korea allege China lied about the death toll, and that its dam construction projects caused the disaster – even though scientists say a glacial collapse in Nepal was to blame.
Online critics also point to the fact that the vast bulk of the dead and missing reported by the two governments are in Nepal.

In Nepal, rescuers have retrieved 1,369 bodies, while around 5,132 people are missing, according to the disaster agency Thursday. In China, the toll is 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media.
The stark difference, however, may be a reflection of the disaster's geography and scale.

The glacial mountain collapse occurred in downstream Nepal, sending a wave of debris so powerful it smashed China's high-altitude border post in tightly restricted Tibet, before carving a path of destruction across Nepal.
Bodies on the Chinese side may have washed downstream too, but because of the geography, they could be buried in a thick layer of mud and debris that makes recovery impossible.
* The writers are from AFP

9c48b1bef0f5670d: PENANG: Gold prices are expected to stay between US$4,000 and US$5,000 an ounce over the next one to two years, the Malaysia Gold Association (MGA) said.

MGA president and Public Gold founder Datuk Seri Louis Ng said gold remained a sought-after asset, but changes in interest rates in major economies could affect investment demand and the precious metal's price direction.

"Gold, I think, will be stable within the US$4,000 to US$5,000 per ounce range for the next one to two years until we see the direction of interest rates," he told reporters after the launch of Public Gold's new refinery.
Gold is currently trading at around US$4,350 an ounce.
Ng said movements in interest rates in the United States and Japan, among other factors, would continue to influence investment demand for gold.
Meanwhile, Public Gold's new refinery, located on a 0.461-hectare site within the Batu Kawan Industrial Park, has a built-up area of approximately 4,038.68 sq m.
The facility is designed to refine up to 10 tonnes of precious metals annually, with capacity expandable to between 20 tonnes and 50 tonnes a year as market demand grows.
Ng said the refinery would enable Public Gold to process scrap gold locally instead of sending it overseas, helping to reduce transportation, insurance and refining costs.
He said Public Gold had exported about two tonnes of scrap gold to Hong Kong and Singapore for refining over the past two months.
"With this refinery, which follows international standards, we can refine it here in Malaysia," he said.

The project is also expected to create approximately 1,000 direct jobs, including highly skilled technical and engineering positions, as well as roles in quality assurance, operations and corporate support.

In his speech, Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development Minister Steven Sim said Penang should explore establishing a gold bazaar and storage facility to support its ambition of becoming a regional financial hub.

He said the proposed gold ecosystem would complement Penang's established gold jewellery manufacturing industry, which accounts for about 70 per cent of Malaysia's gold jewellery manufacturing and production.
Sim said the development of a gold bazaar could position Penang as an alternative regional trading centre while strengthening gold's role as a key asset in the state's financial hub ambitions.

057360426188c7ff: KUANTAN: Hazy conditions and reduced visibility were reported in several areas in the state capital today, with all five Air Pollutant Index (API) monitoring stations in Pahang recording unhealthy readings.
At noon, the five stations — Balok Baru and Indera Mahkota in Kuantan, Temerloh, Jerantut and Rompin — recorded readings ranging from 154 to 164, up from 145 to 152 at 7am.
The 164 reading recorded at Indera Mahkota was the highest in Pahang since haze began affecting parts of the country.
As of 4pm yesterday, all five stations recorded good or moderate API readings.
Checks found that several schools in Kuantan had also suspended outdoor co-curricular activities, including physical education lessons.

Meanwhile, Pahang Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim advised residents in affected areas to minimise outdoor activities, avoid open burning and drink enough water to stay hydrated.
"The public must exercise caution when going outdoors and wear masks, especially those in high-risk groups.
"The Department of Environment and local authorities must conduct regular monitoring and step up enforcement to prevent open burning throughout the state," he said.
An API reading of between 0 and 50 is classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous.
7f1b0a56f826d5c9: PUTRAJAYA: The Northern Corridor Economic Region (NCER) is exploring opportunities in the electric vehicle (EV) and automotive sectors as part of efforts to diversify investments beyond its strong electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor base.

Northern Corridor Implementation Authority chief executive Datuk Mohamad Haris Kader Sultan said it had yet to determine the specific portion of its RM470 billion cumulative investment target by 2030 that could come from the automotive sector, but several potential investments were currently being assessed.

"Among them are high-technology vehicle projects in Kulim, Kedah, with potential investors in the EV sector undergoing due diligence," he said, adding that NCER is also working with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority and the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry to assess the potential investments.
Mohamad Haris said so far, two investors have been identified in the EV battery segment, while three are being considered in the automobile segment.

He also said the move comes as E&E and semiconductor activities continue to form the mainstay of investments in the NCER, particularly in Penang, where about 95 per cent of investments are expected to be concentrated in the sector.

Earlier, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir launched the NCER 2026-2030 Strategic Development Plan here, which aims to realise a cumulative investment of RM470 billion by 2030 with 70 per cent of it contributed by key sectors such as electrical and electronics, automotive, high-value tourism and modern agriculture.
The target is RM126.2 billion higher than the RM343.8 billion under the previous NCER development plan.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Haris said the focus on E&E and semiconductors would not exclude opportunities in other sectors, with efforts also being made to spread growth beyond existing investment centres.
In Kedah, he said Kulim Hi-Tech Park remains among the key areas for investments, while Perlis has Chuping Valley, with semiconductor activities continuing to be a major attraction.
The diversification of investments is also aimed at ensuring that economic growth reaches less-developed areas across the four NCER states -- Perlis, Kedah, Penang and Perak.

He said the programmes and projects would be implemented in these areas to create employment opportunities, including by ensuring that areas developed with allocations from the Economy Ministry are filled with approved investments.

"We are confident of realising our RM470 billion cumulative investment target by 2030, based on approved investments that are expected to be translated into actual projects within two to three years, or up to five years in some cases.

"The target is higher than the previous plan but the projection was supported by investment trends, and our targets for 2020 and 2025 had been exceeded," he said, adding that the investment target is also expected to contribute to NCER's goal of raising median household income to RM7,500 by 2030.

Mohamad Haris also said NCER's approach was not limited to increasing the number of jobs, but also focused on attracting higher-value industries that could generate higher productivity and value-added activities.
About 45 per cent of the jobs targeted are expected to be high-skilled positions.

To meet the demand for skilled workers, NCER is working with local universities, polytechnics, TVET institutions and industry players to identify specific disciplines and skills required by investors.
c5767f03b263c46e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today acquitted former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin of four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd's funds, as the prosecution today said it does not want to proceed with trial on those charges for now.
In this trial, Muhyiddin faced seven charges:

four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and
three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.

Following the High Court's decision after the prosecution's request for a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA), Muhyiddin now only faces three power abuse charges involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin delivered her decision this afternoon on whether to only grant a DNAA or to acquit Muhyiddin on those four charges.
Ultimately, the judge decided to acquit, in the interests of justice.

Just before lunch break today, deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib informed the High Court that the prosecution had decided to not continue with four of the seven charges in Muhyiddin's trial, saying this was after the prosecution had looked at the case as a whole.

"With that, the prosecution respectfully applies for Section 254(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code to be applied, to apply for an order from this court for a DNAA on the accused. We apply for DNAA only on those charges," he said.
Muhyiddin's lawyers had however urged the High Court to acquit Muhyiddin on the four charges related to Bukhary Equity, instead of only granting a DNAA.
80d7ae3ba8d02860: PUTRAJAYA: When a woman involved in a case came to the home of the late Tun Abdul Hamid Mohamad seeking a favour, the former Chief Justice did not hesitate.
He refused the request and told her he would have to withdraw from the case as she should never have approached him.
When she replied that no one would know, his answer was simple.
"God knows."
The story was among the most personal memories shared by Abdul Hamid's daughter, Melati Abdul Hamid, during reference proceedings at the Palace of Justice here today.
For Melati, the brief exchange captured the man her father was — a judge guided by faith, honesty and a deeply held sense of right and wrong.
"As a judge, he did what he believed to be right, to the best of his ability.
"When he sat in court, he decided based purely on the facts adduced and the applicable law. His personal opinion was irrelevant," she said.
She said her father was prepared to do what he believed was right even when it could jeopardise his own future.
Among the decisions she cited were the Federal Court's acquittal of Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2004 and a Special Court decision against a Ruler in 2008.
Melati also recalled a conversation between Abdul Hamid and the late Datuk Tengku Baharuddin Shah Tengku Mahmud, who sat with him on the panel that acquitted Anwar.
Her father had remarked that it was good no one had tried to influence them.
Tengku Baharuddin smiled and replied: "Not to you."
When Abdul Hamid became Chief Justice in 2007, at a time when public trust in the judiciary was low, he knew he had little time before retirement.
His response was characteristically simple.
Two huge banners bearing the words "BUAT KERJA" were hung at the Palace of Justice.
"There were no revolutionary ideas or big reforms.
"The slogan seems simple and obvious, but I believe it is his greatest strength — doing what he is supposed to do, when he is supposed to do it, day in and day out, without fail," said Melati.
Even after retirement and despite worsening health, Abdul Hamid continued writing.
In the final decade of his life, he wrote eight books and hundreds of speeches and articles, typing every word himself and maintaining his own website.
Melati said he wanted the website to remain after his death as his waqf of knowledge.
But to his family, she said, the titles, judgments and books were never the whole story.
"To us, beyond all the titles, judgments, speeches and books, he was simply Ayah."
She recalled a father who cared for his children when their mother worked night shifts, told them stories before bed and joked that having 2 sons and 2 daughters was only fair.
He loved fishing and once told his children that the fish did not care who was holding the rod, or what title that person carried.
In the end, Melati said the message he left to his family and those in the judicial system was the same one he had lived by.
"Buat Kerja.
"Keep your dignity. Never beg or lobby for any position.
"Eventually, honesty supersedes all.
"Eventually, the truth will always prevail."
Her father, she said, remained humble, hardworking, principled and honest.

6b29db8f5dbcad5c: WHAT happens to neurodivergent adults when the parents who have cared for them for decades grow old themselves?

This is an increasingly important question for Malaysian families as the country's population ages, yet long-term planning for neurodivergent individuals is often still centred on childhood intervention rather than the entire lifespan.

To address this issue, the Malaysian Healthy Ageing Society (MHAS), in collaboration with Oasis Place, will bring together healthcare professionals, caregivers, advocates, legal practitioners and neurodivergent adults in a forum entitled The Next Chapter: Planning for Neurodivergent Lives and Ageing Families.
MHAS vice-president Dr Wong Teck Wee says neurodivergence is a lifelong continuum that requires society to rethink how support should be planned.

"Neurodivergence is a lifelong continuum that evolves across the human lifespan, requiring us to shift our focus from acute childhood intervention to sustainable, long-term planning for ageing families."
Building a truly inclusive society means ensuring neurodivergent individuals receive the dignity, care and robust support networks they need at every single stage of life, he adds.
The forum will feature a keynote presentation called "Ageing Through a Neuroaffirmative Lens", by Dr Bill Wong, an occupational therapist and autistic individual.

Two panel discussions titled "When Parents Age Too: Who Plans for Whom?" and "Ageing at Home: Building Your Circle of Support" will also explore the practical challenges families face as they navigate the next stage of life:

Speakers include consultant child and adolescent psychiatrist Dr Albert Lee Muh Haur; parent and neurodiversity advocate Jacquelyn Ang; family and probate practitioner and past president of the Association of Women Lawyers Goh Siu Lin and neurodivergent adult CJ Chew.
Founder of Oasis Place Dr Choy Sook Kuen, says ageing should be viewed as a lifelong conversation rather than something addressed only when a person becomes old.

"Ageing is not something we should begin planning for only when a person becomes older — it is a lifelong conversation, particularly for neurodivergent people and people with disabilities whose support needs may evolve across the lifespan," says Dr Choy.

Early planning for parents, siblings and other caregivers is equally important, because "supporting the supporter" is fundamental to ensuring that care remains sustainable, dignified and compassionate across generations, she adds.

The forum will examine issues including ageing in place, changing care needs, family and caregiver support, legal and probate planning, and the importance of building wider circles of support beyond parents.

The forum will be held on Sept 22 at Four Points by Sheraton Kuala Lumpur, Chinatown. For enquiries, contact 6012-364-6109, email info@healthyageing.org, or visit www.healthyageing.org and www.oasisplace.com.my.
22f5b214c5c6a815: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Malaysians largely mirror global views on success, prioritising stable employment and home ownership, yet they place a significantly higher premium on marriage and parenthood as life milestones, according to a new Ipsos report.

The Ipsos Life Aspirations 2026 report reveals that two in three Malaysians view stability and security as the primary markers of a successful life. Specifically, 67 per cent of Malaysians identify a stable job as essential, compared to 65 per cent globally, while 60 per cent view home ownership as a key milestone, slightly above the global average of 58 per cent.
The findings, based on a survey of 501 Malaysians aged 18 to 74, highlight a clear cultural emphasis on family.
Parenthood and marriage are viewed as markers of success by 47 per cent and 42 per cent of Malaysians, respectively, far outpacing global figures of 31 per cent and 25 per cent.

However, a generational divide is emerging. While the fundamentals of success remain broadly similar, Gen Z Malaysians are placing less emphasis on traditional family milestones than their Millennial counterparts.

Both generations agree on the primacy of career stability, with 69 per cent of Millennials and 68 per cent of Gen Z citing a full-time, stable job as the most important marker of success. Home ownership follows closely, cited by 64 per cent of Millennials and 55 per cent of Gen Z.

The gap in family aspirations is more pronounced: only 32 per cent of Gen Z respondents view marriage as a marker of success, compared to 58 per cent of Millennials. Similarly, only 35 per cent of Gen Z value parenthood as a milestone, against 50 per cent of Millennials.

Ipsos Malaysia managing director Arun Menon noted that this shift aligns with wider demographic trends, as Malaysians increasingly delay marriage and parenthood in favour of education, career progression, and financial security.

The most striking disparity, however, lies in home ownership. While 79 per cent of respondents aspire to own a home, only 46 per cent have achieved this goal, underscoring the persistent affordability crisis in the local housing market.
“Around three in four Malaysians aspire to own a home, yet fewer than half have achieved it, echoing the wider affordability challenges in Malaysia’s housing market,” Arun said.

He added that these findings suggest younger Malaysians are not necessarily redefining success, but are instead reordering their priorities, securing financial and personal stability before pursuing traditional life milestones.
2ca35b8633e9778b: KUALA LUMPUR: All 226.37 million Malaysia Steel Works (KL) Bhd (Masteel) warrants issued five years ago remain unexercised with barely a month until they expire, as the steelmaker's shares trade at about half their exercise price.

9f2cd9b61ecaa15b: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin has been acquitted of three money laundering charges and one abuse of power charge linked to Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Nurdin gave the acquittal after deputy public prosecutor Ahmad Akram Gharib applied for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA).
The three money laundering charges involved Muhyiddin’s receipt of RM200 million from Bukhary Equity while the abuse of power charge had to do with him soliciting the amount from the firm.
The judge said the prosecution offered no reason for the DNAA application, saying only that they did not wish to proceed with the charges.

"Therefore, I am of the view that in the interest of justice, the discretion of the court is to be exercised in favour of the accused, and that is to order him to be discharged and acquitted (of the four charges)," said Ruwena.
Earlier, Akram told the court that the prosecution decided not to proceed with the four charges after reviewing the overall circumstances of the case.
"Accordingly, the prosecution is applying to invoke Section 254(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code and seeking an order from the court for the accused to be granted a DNAA," he said.
He said the application only concerned the four Bukhary Equity charges, not the three other abuse of power charges linked to the Jana Wibawa programme.
Muhyiddin's defence counsel, Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, urged the court to acquit his client of all four charges, saying it was clear that the prosecution was no longer interested in pursuing the charges.
"Today is probably the second last day of the trial, and not a single shred of evidence was produced and no witness statements served on us by the prosecution in respect of these four charges.
"What's most important is that no cogent reasons were advanced by the prosecution as to why they wanted a DNAA, and the law is very clear: strong reasons must be given.
"Otherwise, the court has no choice whatsoever but to grant a discharge amounting to an acquittal," he said.
The prosecution is nearing the close of its case against Muhyiddin over three other abuse of power charges linked to Jana Wibawa.
In that case, he is accused of abusing his position to solicit RM25.3 million in bribes from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Mamfor Sdn Bhd, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and its managing director Azman Yusoff.
8efd8fef75e2b537: WASHINGTON: Detainees at the now-shuttered immigration facility in Florida known as "Alligator Alcatraz" were held at times in metal cages the size of phone booths, according to a new report.
The report by the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) found that the detention centre did not meet standards in a number of areas.

The facility in the Florida Everglades operated by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which became a symbol of President Donald Trump's mass deportation drive, was shut down in June amid legal wrangling and controversy over its soaring costs.

Ahead of its closure, "Alligator Alcatraz" drew criticism from lawyers, relatives of detainees and human rights advocates, who accused the government of holding undocumented migrants in harsh conditions and denying them meaningful due process.
The inspector general's report, which was released on Friday, was compiled after a visit by the OIG to the centre, officially known as the Florida Soft-Sided Facility (FSSF), in January.
It found that FSSF did not meet standards in terms of environmental health and safety, medical care, food service, personal hygiene or recreation.

"FSSF did not provide detainees with sufficient living space, creating cramped conditions for detainees who spent most of their time in their housing units, which may harm detainees' physical and mental health," the report said.

Between July 2025 and January 2026, 79 detainees were confined in small metal enclosures comprising about 1.67 square metres of floor space for periods ranging from several minutes to nearly two hours, the report said.
The enclosures were described by facility staff as "'calming areas' for detainees to deescalate and have time alone," it said.
"Use of these small metal enclosures for any reason is unprecedented among detention facilities OIG has inspected and presents significant risks to detainee health and safety," the report said.
"The use of such restrictive spaces is highly unconventional and does not align with standards for humane treatment."
Among the recommendations made in the report was putting an end to the use of the small metal enclosures, greater access to showers for inmates and more recreation time.

Trump, who has vowed to deport millions of undocumented migrants, visited "Alligator Alcatraz" after its July 2025 opening, boasting about the harsh conditions and joking that the reptilian predators in nearby waters would serve as guards to discourage escape attempts.

09aa1ddd3cdecaee: SINGAPORE: Singapore was shrouded in haze on Tuesday, with smoke from wildfires in neighboring Indonesia raising islandwide pollution to levels that pose a health risk.
All five regions of the city-state recorded unhealthy air-quality levels, the first time that’s happened since September 2019, according to the National Environment Agency.
Singapore’s air currently ranks among the 10 most polluted cities in the world, according to IQAir data, with the capitals of Malaysia and Indonesia also among the top spots.
Indonesia often battles wildfires during its annual dry season, but hotspots this year have been higher than normal.

There were more than 9,000 recorded in August, the most for the month in data going back to 2015, and more than 7,000 have been recorded so far in September, according to the Forestry Ministry’s fire-monitoring platform SiPongi.
The situation is being exacerbated by the strengthening El Niño weather pattern, which causes drier weather in much of the region.

Little immediate relief is expected from the weather, with dry conditions expected to persist across much of the south of Southeast Asia in the near term, according to the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre.
“The hotspot and haze situation in the region is expected to remain escalated with a continued risk of transboundary smoke haze,” the centre said in its latest forecast.

Air quality in parts of Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra regions, where the fires are concentrated, was at dangerous or very unhealthy levels as of Tuesday, government data show. Malaysia has also suffered, with choking haze in late August prompting the government to move its leader’s annual National Day speech to an indoor venue. A state of emergency was declared for part of Sarawak state earlier this month.

A hotspot is defined as a location where satellites detect an elevated surface temperature, indicating a potential fire. Slash-and-burn methods used to clear farmland have previously been linked to the fires, and dry undergrowth can also ignite carbon-rich peatland, which can smolder for long periods and be difficult to extinguish.

Smoke plumes from fires in Kalimantan drifted toward Singapore because of a shift in winds, alongside smoke haze from Sumatra, the National Environment Agency said on Monday. The agency expects the haze to persist over the next 24 hours, with air quality ranging from high-moderate to mid-unhealthy conditions.

Indonesia’s forestry ministry said in a statement that this year’s surge in forest fires was due to a combination of El Niño-driven dry weather and human-caused ignition, adding that each incident must be investigated individually. The country has expanded aerial firefighting operations, including with helicopters provided by Japan, it said. Malaysia has also offered assistance to tackle the blazes.

The fires in Indonesia add to a bad year for wildfires globally, with parts of Europe and North America also reeling from recent blazes. The current El Niño has a 75% chance of becoming “a historic event,” surpassing all records dating back to 1950, the US Climate Prediction Center said last week.

There may be a slight uptick in rainfall in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan next week, which could temporarily ease fire risks, according to Takahisa Nishikawa, senior decision support meteorologist at Atmospheric G2.
“This may provide some relief, although it does not yet look like a widespread or sustained wetting pattern, and forecast confidence is lower at that range,” he said.

The dry weather is also affecting the mining and agriculture industries in Indonesia. A nickel producer there said on Tuesday it was halting the ramp-up of one of its processing plants due to water shortages, while the country’s biggest nickel complex warned earlier this month that it might have to slash output for the same reason. Palm oil production is also expected to take a hit as plantations struggle to apply fertilizer.
a0baffe60643e149: PUTRAJAYA: The standards set by four of Malaysia’s former top judicial leaders must continue to guide today’s judges, says Chief Justice Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh.

Speaking at reference proceedings in memory of three former chief justices and a former chief judge of Malaya, Wan Ahmad Farid said the judiciary’s strength was not in its grand buildings or titles but in the character and conduct of those who served it.
"Their chairs are now empty. Their standards remain. And so does our duty to carry the work forward," he said.

He was referring to former chief justices Eusoff Chin, who served from 1994 to 2000; Dzaiddin Abdullah (2002-2003) and Abdul Hamid Mohamad (2007-2008), as well as former chief judge of Malaya Siti Norma Yaakob (2005-2007).
Wan Ahmad Farid said Eusoff, who had the longest tenure as chief justice, left behind a culture of discipline, particularly in ensuring that judges sit on the bench on time.
"Judicial time does not belong to the judge. It belongs to the litigant waiting, sometimes for years, for his or her day in court," he said.

Wan Ahmad Farid said Dzaiddin, the first chief justice appointed from the Bar, inherited a judiciary facing complaints over courtesy, restraint and propriety. His mission was to "put our house in order" and restore public confidence.
"Dzaiddin taught the judiciary to listen again," said Wan Ahmad Farid, adding that Dzaiddin’s openness to technology also paved the way for developments such as online hearings.

Wan Ahmad Farid also highlighted Hamid's strong belief in judicial restraint and the limits of judicial power. Referring to Hamid’s book, Hakim Bukan Parlimen (Judges Are Not Parliament), he said judges were there to interpret the law, not make it.
Hamid’s other message was simply: "buat kerja" – do the work. "Public confidence is earned through competent, often unglamorous duty, mostly outside the headlines," Wan Ahmad Farid added.
He also hailed Norma as a trailblazer who opened doors for women in the legal profession and judiciary, and had the two qualities needed by a judge: "patience and incorruptibility".
Wan Ahmad Farid said incorruptibility went beyond money, requiring judges to be immune to pressure, flattery and favour.
"A litigant should leave knowing that the judge listened, considered the matter fairly and decided without fear or favour. That is how we earn the public’s trust, one case at a time."

Summing up the legacy of the four, Wan Ahmad Farid said Eusoff gave the judiciary discipline, Dzaiddin restored its trust, Hamid gave lasting expression to principle and restraint, and Norma broadened the pool from which judges could be drawn.
"Not one of those four things is sufficient on its own. They have done their part. It now falls to us to do ours for those who come after," he said.

f531ec5ac7805c89: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad today told the High Court that a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer had allegedly attempted to intimidate and tarnish his reputation as a lawyer, based on the officer’s MACC colleague’s police report.
Amer, who was cross-examining MACC officer Mazery Mohd Zaini as the 29th prosecution witness yesterday in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, said the police report had false information.

Amer said the police report lodged yesterday had named him and referred to the ongoing trial, and referred to an alleged classified document that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had wanted to be included as evidence in the trial.

Amer said the MACC officer who lodged the police report had said he received information from the investigating officer in Muhyiddin’s trial, adding that he could only infer that it refers to Mazery who is still under oath and was scheduled to give evidence in court today.
“It’s clearly an attempt at intimidation,” he said. “But I’m not intimidated, they drew first blood and I will repay them with no quarters.”

Amer accused Mazery of trying to tarnish his reputation and trying to mislead the public via the police report’s claim that the document is not related to Muhyiddin’s trial, describing it as an “underhanded tactic” by a witness who was still testifying in court.
The alleged classified document was the statement that MACC had recorded from Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad during investigations.

“No court should condone this kind of tactic. Yang Arif is supposed to decide on subject matter of the case based on all facts and legal arguments. Yet the very IO whom we have challenged with several issues, decided to undermine the entire trial process by lodging this report,” he said.

Amer told the High Court that he is considering various legal action: “I will not exclude the possibility of lodging a report against the appropriate person including the IO for making false report, contempt of court and any other legal action. I reserve all those rights.”
“I’m making an application to this court to reserve my right to further cross this witness with regard to his underhanded tactic,” he added.
